newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Booker sales growth 5-6 pct.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Booker sales growth 5-6 pct.

text.p: Food services company Booker Plc has seen five to six percent like-for-like sales growth in its cash-and-carry business since its year ended December 28, said chief executive Charles Bowen.
About two thirds of the company's overall profits come from cash-and-carry. The like-for-like growth is in line with figures released by Britain's major supermarkets.

"There is a lot to do this year. We are working very hard but we are trying to stop people getting too excited too early. In 1997 we will show a small amount of growth but in 1998 shareholders can expect a significant return," said Bowen in an interview.

He said the stockmarket was forecasting pre-tax profits for Booker of 105 million stg for 1997, after the de-consolidation of its Portugese business, a number which the company would not argue too much with.
"The overall message about this year is there are no surprises we are on track and the year has started as we expected it to."
Earlier, the company posted 1996 pre-tax profits, excluding exceptional items, of 101.9 million stg, up from 100.6 million.
Sales rose 5 percent to 4.443 billion stg.
Exceptional charges totalled 88.9 million, due mainly to the integration of Nurdin and Peacock acquired in November and the reorganisation of Booker Foodservice.
The acquisition of N&P in November created a cash and carry wholesale business with combined sales of 4.0 billion stg and purchasing strength comparable to that of major supermarket groups.
Bowen said Booker still had considerable costs to get out of integrating N&P, representing 10 million stg in the first year and more than twice that by 1999.
As a result of the acquisition Booker is benefitting from an increased purchasing power and savings in distribution, he said.
The expansion of the central distribution project will take longer than expected, however, and will not be completed until the middle of 1998, he said.
The acquisition of Nurdin bought with it 56 depots, generally larger than Booker's, so as Nurdin stock is run down these will be used for food services distribution.
